options: emp is a struct variable, not a pointer; use . for direct access
emp is a pointer; . cannot be used
. and -> are interchangeable
Compiler error: . is not valid for structs
explanation: emp.field accesses a struct member directly; emp->field accesses via a pointer (equiv to (*emp).field).

options: Two separate heap-allocated Node structs linked via pointers
A single contiguous block containing both nodes
Compiler error: recursive struct definitions are invalid
head and head->next point to the same memory
explanation: Each malloc allocates independent memory; next is a pointer linking them, not a contiguous array.

options: -> dereferences the pointer and accesses the member; (*pptr).x explicitly dereferences then uses . (both are equivalent)
They are not equivalent
pptr->x is a shorthand that the compiler expands to (*pptr).x
Compiler error: mixing pointer and direct access
explanation: pptr->x is syntactic sugar for (*pptr).x; the -> operator combines dereference and member access.

options: Union members share the same memory; setting d.i then reading d.f interprets int bits as float (type punning)
Unions cannot store both int and float
d.f is automatically updated when d.i changes
Compiler error: cannot read different members
explanation: Unions overlay members; reading a different member reinterprets the bit pattern.

options: r.point.x accesses the x field of the nested point struct
r.x (nested structs collapse into the parent scope)
Compiler error: nested structs are invalid
r.point->x (nested structs are pointers)
explanation: Nested structs require chained member access; each . accesses a level of nesting.

options: Allocate nodes with malloc; set left/right pointers to link them, using NULL for absent children
Binary trees are built statically; malloc is not used
Nodes are linked via arrays, not pointers
Left and right must be allocated separately from the parent
explanation: Tree nodes are typically dynamically allocated; pointers form the tree structure.

options: top = -1 indicates an empty stack; incrementing gives top = 0 for the first push (items[0])
top must always be negative
A stack is always empty
Compiler error: negative indices are forbidden
explanation: Using top = -1 for empty simplifies push (++top then store) and pop logic.

options: To implement a circular queue; modulo wraps tail/head around when they exceed capacity, reusing space at the start
Modulo prevents overflow
Queues do not wrap; modulo is unnecessary
Compiler error: modulo on array indices
explanation: Circular queues reuse array space by wrapping indices; modulo 10 cycles through the 10-element buffer.

options: Multiple keys hash to the same index; entries overwrite each other (open addressing or chaining needed to resolve)
Hash tables never collide
Compiler error: collisions are not allowed
Arrays cannot be used for hash tables
explanation: Hash collisions are inevitable; resolution strategies include chaining (linked lists) or probing (seek next free slot).

options: Each index is a node; the linked list at adjacency[i] stores edges from node i (each edge has destination and weight)
Edges are stored in a separate array
Graphs cannot be represented with pointers
Compiler error: nested structs and pointers are invalid
explanation: Adjacency lists efficiently represent sparse graphs; each node's list tracks outgoing edges.
